title: Marine & the Sea
description: Ships, storms, and the sublime power of the ocean across the centuries.
source: Art Institute of Chicago, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Wikimedia Commons

items.title: A State Yacht and Other Craft in Calm Water
items.description_narrative: Ornate sailing vessels with patterned pennants ride at anchor on glassy water, small rowboats crowded with passengers ferrying between them under a pale, cloud-streaked sky. Jan van de Cappelle painted this scene around 1660; it belongs to the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: sailing ships, calm water, dutch golden age, marine art, van de cappelle, oil painting
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Snow Storm: Steam-Boat off a Harbour's Mouth
items.description_narrative: A steamship is swallowed by swirling snow and spray, its mast and a trailing plume of dark smoke barely visible through the storm. Turner painted this in 1842; the Tate now holds it.
items.tags: storm, steamship, snow, marine art, turner, oil painting, sublime

items.title: The Shipwreck
items.description_narrative: Small boats crowded with survivors pitch on mountainous dark waves beneath a bruised, stormy sky, one boat's pale sail catching the only light. J. M. W. Turner painted this shipwreck scene in 1805; it is held at Tate Britain.
items.tags: shipwreck, storm, seascape, turner, marine art, survivors, romanticism

items.title: Dutch Boats in a Gale
items.description_narrative: A small fishing boat heels hard under a straining pale sail, its crew hauling at the ropes as dark water piles into whitecaps around the hull. Behind it, ordinary ships shrink to silhouettes beneath a towering, sunlit thundercloud. J. M. W. Turner painted the scene in 1801; it hangs today in the National Gallery.
items.tags: seascape, storm, sailing ship, romanticism, turner, oil painting, dramatic sky
items.credit_line: The Yorck Project (2002) 10.000 Meisterwerke der Malerei (DVD-ROM), distributed by DIRECTMEDIA Publishing GmbH. ISBN: 3936122202.

items.title: Breezing Up (A Fair Wind)
items.description_narrative: Spray flies from the bow as a man and three boys crowd a small sailboat heeling sharply under full sail, its name painted across the stern. Homer painted this in 1873; the National Gallery of Art now holds it.
items.tags: sailing, catboat, boys, marine art, winslow homer, oil painting
items.credit_line: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

items.title: The Fog Warning
items.description_narrative: A great halibut fills the bow of a lone fisherman's dory as he rows hard through choppy water, a distant white sail barely visible against the hazy sky. Homer painted this in 1885; it is now in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
items.tags: fisherman, rowboat, marine art, realism, winslow homer, oil painting, fog

items.title: Northeaster
items.description_narrative: A wall of white foam bursts over dark rocks as a wave rears beneath a heavy, colorless sky. Winslow Homer painted this scene in the 1890s; it belongs to the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: wave, rocky coast, storm, marine art, winslow homer, oil painting, seascape
items.credit_line: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (The Met object ID 20011487)

items.title: Eight Bells
items.description_narrative: Two sailors in broad-brimmed oilskins stand shoulder to shoulder on a rolling deck, each sighting a brass instrument toward a churning grey sea beneath heavy clouds. Homer painted this in 1886; the Addison Gallery of American Art holds it today.
items.tags: sailors, marine art, realism, navigation, winslow homer, oil painting, overcast sky
items.credit_line: 1. about.com2. Addison Gallery of American Art

items.title: The Ninth Wave
items.description_narrative: A towering wave, its crest blazing orange-and-gold as the low sun burns through storm clouds, rears above survivors clinging to makeshift wreckage. Aivazovsky dated this dramatic seascape 1850; the Russian Museum now holds it.
items.tags: shipwreck, survivors, storm, sunrise, aivazovsky, oil painting, dramatic sky

items.title: The Black Sea
items.description_narrative: A grand fleet of tall-masted warships rides at anchor in a calm bay ringed by hills, their reflections rippling across pale blue water beneath a hazy sky. Ivan Aivazovsky is credited as the artist.
items.tags: fleet, sailing ships, bay, calm water, aivazovsky, marine art

items.title: A Dutch Ship in a Strong Breeze
items.agent_name: Willem van de Velde the Younger
items.description_narrative: A tall flagged warship leans under billowing sail as smaller fishing boats ride the chop beneath a bank of grey cloud. Willem van de Velde the Younger painted this marine scene in 1658; it now hangs in the National Gallery.
items.tags: marine art, sailing ship, dutch golden age, seascape, van de velde, oil painting

items.title: Ships in a Stormy Sea
items.description_narrative: Tall ships pitch through mountainous waves in fine grey linework, one listing dangerously as smaller boats scatter beneath a churning, cloud-filled sky. Ludolf Bakhuizen made this ink drawing in 1698; it belongs to the Albertina.
items.tags: sailing ships, storm, drawing, ink, bakhuizen, dutch golden age, dramatic waves

items.title: Ships in Distress off a Rocky Coast
items.description_narrative: Ships heel and founder among towering rock outcrops as a churning green sea and a storm-lit sky frame the scene, a broken mast floating in the foreground. Ludolf Bakhuizen painted this stormy coastal scene in 1667.
items.tags: shipwreck, rocky coast, storm, marine art, bakhuizen, oil painting, dramatic sky

items.title: The Monk by the Sea
items.description_narrative: A solitary robed figure stands on a pale dune, dwarfed by a vast, empty expanse of dark sea and roiling grey sky. Caspar David Friedrich painted this scene around 1808; it belongs to the Alte Nationalgalerie.
items.tags: solitude, seascape, romanticism, sublime, caspar david friedrich, oil painting, minimal

items.title: The Stormy Sea
items.description_narrative: Two small wooden boats sit beached on a dark shore as a massive green wave curls and breaks just beyond them under a sky heavy with grey clouds. Gustave Courbet is credited as the artist; the image is dated 1869.
items.tags: stormy sea, boats, wave, shoreline, courbet, oil painting
items.credit_line: Photo taken by Jaime Villate on 2009-08-04 at Orsay Museum.

items.title: Calm Sea
items.description_narrative: A vast pale sky filled with soft grey clouds presses down on a narrow band of turquoise sea and an empty stretch of sand. Gustave Courbet is credited as the artist; the image is dated 1866.
items.tags: seascape, minimal, sky, calm water, courbet, oil painting
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: Brig upon the Water
items.description_narrative: A brig sails in silhouette against a luminous, cloud-streaked sky, its reflection glowing on calm water rendered in warm sepia tones. Gustave Le Gray made this photograph in 1856.
items.tags: photograph, sailing ship, silhouette, sepia, le gray, seascape

items.title: The Icebergs
items.description_narrative: Painted in 1861, Church's towering ice cliffs glow gold and white against a smoky sky, their sheer faces mirrored in still, dark water below; the Dallas Museum of Art now holds the canvas.
items.tags: iceberg, arctic, landscape, hudson river school, church, oil painting, sublime

items.title: The Gulf Stream
items.description_narrative: Sharks circle through churning turquoise water around a lone man reclining in a battered, mastless boat, a distant ship and waterspout on the horizon. Homer painted this in 1899; it hangs today in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: sharks, shipwreck, peril, marine art, winslow homer, oil painting, open sea
items.credit_line: 1. The Yorck Project (2002) 10.000 Meisterwerke der Malerei (DVD-ROM), distributed by DIRECTMEDIA Publishing GmbH. ISBN: 3936122202. 2. art database

items.title: The Wave (La Vague)
items.description_narrative: A dark, wind-whipped wave curls and foams close against the viewer, filling the whole scene beneath a bruised, cloud-choked sky with no shore in sight. Gustave Courbet is credited as the artist; it belongs to the Dallas Museum of Art.
items.tags: wave, storm, close-up, seascape, courbet, oil painting

items.title: The Battle of Trafalgar
items.description_narrative: A towering three-decked warship dominates the canvas, sails torn and signal flags streaming, while sailors in a crowded rowboat look on amid smoke and wreckage. J. M. W. Turner painted this view of the Battle of Trafalgar in the 1820s; it hangs at the National Maritime Museum, part of Royal Museums Greenwich.
items.tags: naval battle, warship, turner, royal navy, romanticism, history painting

items.title: Fishermen at Sea
items.description_narrative: This early Turner seascape, fishermen huddled around a lantern as jagged rock spires rise from the mist and pale light silvers the swell, dates to 1796 and hangs today at the Tate.
items.tags: fishermen, night scene, marine art, romanticism, turner, oil painting, rocky coast

items.title: Rockets and Blue Lights (Close at Hand) to Warn Steamboats of Shoal Water
items.description_narrative: On a wet shoreline, figures gather as a fiery light streaks upward and reflects on the sand, ships barely visible through a churning, cloud-choked sky. Turner painted this in 1840; the Clark Art Institute now holds it.
items.tags: shoreline, flare, ships, marine art, turner, oil painting, dramatic sky

items.title: Calais Pier
items.description_narrative: Sailing boats pitch through churning waves beneath a dramatic, storm-lit sky as figures crowd a wooden pier in the foreground. J. M. W. Turner painted this marine scene at Calais in 1803; it is held by the National Gallery in London.
items.tags: seascape, storm, pier, sailing ship, turner, romanticism, marine art
items.credit_line: National Gallery, London, NG472; Wikidata Q3794814

items.title: Peace – Burial at Sea
items.description_narrative: A dark-hulled ship glows with an eerie reflected fire on the water, black sails and rigging stark against a pale, smoky sky. Turner painted this funeral scene in 1842; it is now in the collection of Tate Britain.
items.tags: funeral, ship, night scene, marine art, turner, oil painting, somber

items.title: Beach Scene, Trouville
items.description_narrative: Eugène Boudin painted this beach scene in the 1870s. Elegant visitors in long skirts and top hats sit and stand near beach chairs beneath fluttering flags, small dogs at their feet, while sailboats glide on the water and steamship smoke rises along the horizon.
items.tags: boudin, marine painting, beach scene, trouville, normandy, impressionism, sailboats, oil painting
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: Perry's Victory on Lake Erie
items.description_narrative: Sailing warships trade cannon fire in billowing smoke, their masts crowded with rigging, one flying a flag of stars and stripes against a pastel evening sky. Thomas Birch painted this naval battle scene around 1814; it belongs to the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts.
items.tags: naval battle, warship, war of 1812, lake erie, thomas birch, marine art
items.credit_line: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts; Wikidata Q110763733
items.current_repository: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts

items.title: Lumber Schooners at Evening on Penobscot Bay
items.description_narrative: A two-masted schooner rides at anchor on calm water as the last pink light of sunset fades behind low hills, a second small sail visible in the distance. Fitz Henry Lane painted this in 1863; the National Gallery of Art now holds it.
items.tags: schooner, sunset, marine art, luminism, fitz henry lane, oil painting, calm water
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: Grey and Silver: Old Battersea Reach
items.description_narrative: Small boats and barges crowd a hazy river beneath smoking factory chimneys, the whole scene softened to greys and silvers. Whistler painted this in 1863; the Art Institute of Chicago now holds it.
items.tags: river scene, barges, tonalism, industrial, whistler, oil painting, hazy

items.title: Coast Scene, Bathers
items.description_narrative: Tiny figures wade and stroll along a strip of sand beneath a sky and sea rendered almost as one soft grey-green wash. James McNeill Whistler distilled a crowded beach into a few dabs of paint in the 1880s. The panel now belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.
items.tags: beach, bathers, tonalism, seascape, whistler, oil on panel, muted palette

items.title: Nocturne: Blue and Gold—Southampton Water
items.description_narrative: A hazy golden moon hangs low over still, dark water dotted with the faint silhouettes of small boats and distant masts. Whistler titled this nocturne in 1872; the Art Institute of Chicago now holds it.
items.tags: nocturne, night scene, tonalism, seascape, whistler, oil painting, tranquil

items.title: Capture of the Tripoli by the Enterprise
items.description_narrative: Two schooners run close together under full pale sail, a small red pennant snapping from the masthead as dark storm clouds mass behind them. Thomas Birch painted this naval scene around 1806; it belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.
items.tags: naval battle, schooners, sailing ships, marine art, thomas birch, oil painting
